title: reduce(into:) to Build a Histogram
hints: `reduce(into:)` mutates one accumulator instead of copying it every step.
Start with an empty dictionary and append each word under its length.
jsBridge: `reduce(into: [:]) { acc, x in acc[k, default: []].append(x) }` mutates the accumulator in place. JS `reduce` with `{...acc}` spread copies every step (O(n²)). Swift's plain `reduce` has the same copying risk, so reach for `into:`.

compass.q: The JS pattern `reduce((acc, x) => ({...acc, [k]: …}), {})` is O(n²). How does `reduce(into:)` avoid that?
